rule: row r = the barrel tilted pitch_deg[r] degrees DOWN (negative = raised); cell k in a row = ground bearing 11.25k (0 = down-right on screen, 45 = at the viewer); pivot in each cell's middle. aim_deg, muzzle, ground_deg, aim_len are [row][cell]. Row 0 (22 up, the same as strip32 and the still) is the fixed tilt.
aim_rule: The barrel keeps one tilt (owner, 28 Oct) and turns only left and right: the game shows the cell whose ground bearing is nearest the target's, and works out the shell's arc from that cell's muzzle to the target, so the shot does not have to leave along the barrel's line.
note: body parts standing in front of the barrel are already cut out of each cell, so no front layer is needed; the ring of spikes sits below the barrel, so it never passes through them. strip32 (32 headings, barrel raised 22 degrees, one row) stays as it was.
aim_note: aim_deg: on-screen direction the barrel points (0 = right, 90 = down), measured from the 3D model; muzzle: [dx, dy] game px from the pivot to the muzzle tip on screen; ground_deg: on-screen direction of the cell's heading on the ground; aim_len: barrel length on screen in game px (short = pointing at or away from the viewer).
